## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design a dynamic geometric structure with deletions, leveraging offline time decomposition and per-node hull maintenance. Requires reasoning about intervals, convex hull construction, and multi-node query aggregation.

## Key Concepts

- Offline dynamic geometry using a segment tree over time
- Per-node 2D convex hulls for max dot product queries
- Handling deletions via time intervals; duplicates via multiplicities

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudocode sketch
class Node { constructor() { this.points = []; this.hull = null; } build() { this.hull = buildHull(this.points); } maxDot(w) { return this.hull ? this.hull.maxDot(w) : -Infinity; } }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you handle numeric precision in maxDot, especially with near-collinear points?
- How would you adapt to support dynamic updates to W (non-static query vector) efficiently?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to combine range data structures for multi-criteria queries and a k-th statistic within a range. It exposes memory vs. time trade-offs and handling of duplicates.

## Key Concepts
- Segment tree over time domain
- Fenwick trees at nodes for weight counts
- Coordinate compression of timestamps and weights
- Range sum and k-th order statistics within a range
- Handling duplicates via counts

## Code Example
```javascript
class EventDS {
  insertEvent(ts, w) {}
  eraseEvent(ts, w) {}
  rangeSum(a, b) { return 0; }
  findKthWeightInRange(a, b, k) { return -1; }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you support unbounded timestamps?
- What are memory/time trade-offs vs. a wavelet tree alternative?
- How would you parallelize queries across cores for large workloads?
